traits.note: FNA vol. 28, Hypnum (Schofield; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants yellowish, green or brown, glossy or dull; stems creeping, pinnate or irregularly branched; leaves secund or falcate-secund; seta yellowish to reddish; capsule usually curved. Typical values are H. cupressiforme of roofs, walls and trunks (same volume): rusty, golden or yellow-green; stems 1-8 cm, creeping, irregularly pinnate; leaves 1.5-2 x 0.5-0.8 mm, falcate-secund; seta reddish 1-2.5 cm; capsule slightly inclined, reddish, cylindric, 1.8-2.5 mm; dioicous. Wikipedia, Hypnum cupressiforme (read 2026-11-05): smooth dense mats on trunks, logs, walls and rocks, preferring acid surfaces.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A creeping mat's depth above its surface, not its shoots' length: a few millimetres, as the leaves lie in a few layers over the creeping stems.

traits.light.note: Bryophyte Biology p. 276 (card bryo-p276-4): most bryophytes are plants of shade; H. cupressiforme mats are thickest on the shaded sides of roofs, walls and trunks (general bryological knowledge).

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate: pleurocarps add one to two centimetres of shoot a year at the mat's edge. To check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology, vol. 1, chapter 5.

traits.operculum_form.note: FNA vol. 28, Hypnum: operculum conic to rounded-mammillate (H. cupressiforme conic to rostrate). (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (H. cupressiforme, one Washington photo, r/g 0.91; b/g 0.18, between it and the mats of Kindbergia oregana and Homalothecium). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.
